source_description: NASA GMAO MERRA-2, redistributed and regridded by the GEOS-Chem team at 4 degrees latitude by 5 degrees longitude. These profiles are coarse regional model estimates, not local measurements. The download uses native-model-layer files, not the 42-pressure-level collection originally considered.
height_method: Height above the model surface is derived hydrostatically from temperature, specific humidity, surface pressure and the GEOS 72-layer pressure coefficients. Heights are estimates, not directly downloaded height observations. The demo stops at the highest layer center below 60 km.
time_method: T, QV and PS linearly interpolated halfway between 00:00 and 03:00 UTC instantaneous fields. U and V are 00:00-03:00 UTC means centered at 01:30. These are not simultaneous direct observations.

thermal_layer_method.tropopause: Lowest sampled level from 5 to 22 km above model surface with forward lapse rate <=2 K/km and mean lapse rates to ALL higher levels within 2 km <=2 K/km. Piecewise-linear temperature, including the exact 2 km endpoint. First lapse-rate tropopause estimate only; no secondary tropopauses. Search floor excludes shallow boundary-layer inversions.
thermal_layer_method.stratopause: Warmest sampled level from 35 to 58 km, only if an interior local maximum with cooler temperatures 2 km below and above. No spline or invented 50 km boundary. Adjacent model centers bracket sampling resolution, not a statistical confidence interval. An elevated or ambiguous stratopause outside this search cannot be diagnosed.
thermal_layer_method.geometry: All heights above model surface. Shell radius = Earth radius + height times 40; identical height scaling for shells and acoustic rays. The selected regional column is extended uniformly around the globe as a schematic; it is not a measured global boundary map. Layer opacity and color are illustrative, not density measurements. Surface to the lowest center is unobserved; lower-zone shading extends to surface.

model: Flat, horizontally uniform, dry-air effective-speed ray approximation: c_eff=sqrt(1.4*287.05*T)+U*sin(bearing)+V*cos(bearing). Analytic integration through piecewise-linear effective speed. No crosswind advection, terrain, Earth curvature, absorption or amplitude prediction.
audio_note: Source cue and distant receiver arrival are combined for presentation. This is not an echo heard at the source. Arrival time is divided by 1000; the musical clip is not sped up. Return amplitude is artistic, not predicted. Infrasound-inspired ray paths do not validate audible bell propagation.
